title: Describing and judging
goal: Use adjectives correctly — including 很, which doesn't mean "very" — give opinions with 觉得, and stop putting 是 where it doesn't belong.
bekal: give opinions with 觉得 and 认为
use 太…了, 真, 非常, 不太
describe people, places, food and weather

dialogs.title: 对话 1 — How's the city?
dialogs.intro: Andi has been in Beijing for a month. Wang Li asks about his impressions. Notice that there's hardly a single 是 in this whole conversation — even though it's full of "this is like this, that is like that".

lines.speaker: 王丽:
lines.text: [北京|Běijīng][怎么样|zěnmeyàng]？[你|Nǐ][习惯|xíguàn][吗|ma]？
lines.id: How's Beijing? Are you used to it?
lines.literal: Beijing — how. you — accustomed — (question).

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [北京|Běijīng][很|hěn][大|dà]，[也|yě][很|hěn][有意思|yǒu yìsi]。
lines.id: Beijing is big, and interesting.
lines.literal: Beijing — (prop) — big, also — (prop) — have — meaning.

lines.speaker: 王丽:
lines.text: [天气|Tiānqì][呢|ne]？[印尼|Yìnní][没有|méiyǒu][冬天|dōngtiān][吧|ba]？
lines.id: And the weather? Indonesia doesn't have winter, right?
lines.literal: weather — (and?). Indonesia — not-have — winter — right.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [对|Duì]。[这儿|Zhèr][冬天|dōngtiān][太|tài][冷|lěng][了|le]！[我|Wǒ][很|hěn][不|bù][习惯|xíguàn]。
lines.id: Right. Winter here is way too cold! I'm really not used to it.
lines.literal: correct. here — winter — too — cold — (change). I — (prop) — not — accustomed.

lines.speaker: 王丽:
lines.text: [菜|Cài][怎么样|zěnmeyàng]？[你|Nǐ][觉得|juéde][好吃|hǎochī][吗|ma]？
lines.id: How's the food? Do you think it's good?
lines.literal: dish — how. you — feel — good-to-eat — (question).

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [非常|Fēicháng][好吃|hǎochī]！[但是|Dànshì][有点儿|yǒudiǎnr][辣|là]。
lines.id: Really delicious! But a bit spicy.
lines.literal: very — good-to-eat. but — have-a-bit — spicy.

lines.speaker: 王丽:
lines.text: [北京菜|Běijīng cài][不|bù][辣|là][啊|a]。[你|Nǐ][吃|chī][的|de][是|shì][四川菜|Sìchuān cài][吧|ba]？
lines.id: Beijing food isn't spicy, though. What you ate was Sichuan food, right?
lines.literal: Beijing — dish — not — spicy — (softener). you — eat — (of) — be — Sichuan — dish — right.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [可能|Kěnéng][是|shì]。[我|Wǒ][觉得|juéde][中国菜|Zhōngguó cài][比|bǐ][印尼菜|Yìnní cài][油|yóu]。
lines.id: Maybe. I think Chinese food is oilier than Indonesian food.
lines.literal: maybe — be. I — feel — China — dish — compared-to — Indonesia — dish — oily.

lines.speaker: 王丽:
lines.text: [有|Yǒu][一点儿|yìdiǎnr][道理|dàolǐ]。[人|Rén][呢|ne]？[北京人|Běijīng rén][怎么样|zěnmeyàng]？
lines.id: You have a point. And the people? What are Beijingers like?
lines.literal: have — a-little — reason. people — (and?). Beijing — people — how.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [很|Hěn][热情|rèqíng]，[说话|shuōhuà][很|hěn][快|kuài]。[我|Wǒ][常常|chángcháng][听|tīng][不|bù][懂|dǒng]。
lines.id: Very friendly, and they talk fast. I often can't follow.
lines.literal: (prop) — warm-feeling, speak — (prop) — fast. I — often — hear — not — understand.

notes: **⚠️ Adjective sentences do NOT use 是.** [北京很大|Běijīng hěn dà] = Beijing is big. Not 北京是大. This is the number-one mistake English speakers make — "is" seems to need a translation — and it lasts for years unless you root it out now. **是 only links a noun to a noun.**

**⚠️ [很|hěn] in adjective sentences does NOT mean "very".** It's an empty prop that has to be there so the sentence doesn't sound like a comparison. [他很高|Tā hěn gāo] simply means "he's tall", not "he's very tall". Drop 很 — [他高|Tā gāo] — and it sounds like "HE's the tall one (not the other)".

**If you really mean "very", use another word**: [非常|fēicháng] very, [真|zhēn] really, [太…了|tài… le] too, [特别|tèbié] especially. You can also stress 很 with your voice — that's exactly how native speakers do it.
**[觉得|juéde] = feel, think.** [我觉得很好|Wǒ juéde hěn hǎo] I think it's good. It softens any opinion and is used constantly — far more often than [认为|rènwéi], which feels formal.
**[怎么样|zěnmeyàng]？ asks for a judgment.** [北京怎么样|Běijīng zěnmeyàng]？ How's Beijing? Don't confuse it with [怎么|zěnme], which asks about **method**: [怎么去|zěnme qù]？ how do I get there?
**[吧|ba] at the end can also mean "right?"** — a guess asking for confirmation. [你是中国人吧|Nǐ shì Zhōngguó rén ba]？ You're Chinese, right?

**[听不懂|tīng bu dǒng] = hear but not understand.** This is a potential complement, HSK 3 material. Recognize it for now: [听懂|tīngdǒng] understand (by listening), [听不懂|tīng bu dǒng] can't follow, [看不懂|kàn bu dǒng] can't understand what you're reading.

grammars.title: Adjective sentences — a frame that must really stick
after: ⚠️ Look at rows two and three: **很 appears only in plain positive sentences.** As soon as the sentence is negated, turned into a question, or given another intensifier, 很 vanishes. That's the clearest proof it's just a prop, not a word with meaning.
⚠️ Don't stack intensifiers: 很非常好 and 太很好了 are both wrong. Pick one.

grammars.title: Giving opinions

head: Pattern
Example
Nuance
rows: [我觉得这个很贵|Wǒ juéde zhège hěn guì]。
[我认为他是对的|Wǒ rènwéi tā shì duì de]。
I believe — formal, used in writing
[我想他不会来|Wǒ xiǎng tā bú huì lái]。
[对我来说，中文很难|Duì wǒ lái shuō, Zhōngwén hěn nán]。
What do you think? — handing the opinion back

after: Negating an opinion: **put 不 on 觉得, not inside the content.** [我不觉得很贵|Wǒ bù juéde hěn guì] "I don't think it's expensive" sounds much gentler than [我觉得不贵|Wǒ juéde bú guì]. English works exactly the same way.

dialogs.title: 对话 2 — Weather and feelings
dialogs.intro: A month later, on a scorching day. Weather is safe small talk anywhere, and you'll need its adjectives every day.

lines.speaker: 李明:
lines.text: [今天|Jīntiān][真|zhēn][热|rè][啊|a]！[三十八|Sānshíbā][度|dù]！
lines.id: It's so hot today! Thirty-eight degrees!
lines.literal: today — really — hot — (exclamation). thirty-eight — degree.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [印尼|Yìnní][也|yě][热|rè]，[但是|dànshì][没有|méiyǒu][这么|zhème][热|rè]。
lines.id: Indonesia's hot too, but not this hot.
lines.literal: Indonesia — also — hot, but — not-have — this — hot.

lines.speaker: 李明:
lines.text: [北京|Běijīng][夏天|xiàtiān][很|hěn][热|rè]，[冬天|dōngtiān][很|hěn][冷|lěng]。[春天|Chūntiān][最|zuì][舒服|shūfu]。
lines.id: Beijing summers are hot and winters are cold. Spring is the most pleasant.
lines.literal: Beijing — summer — (prop) — hot, winter — (prop) — cold. spring — most — comfortable.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [明天|Míngtiān][天气|tiānqì][怎么样|zěnmeyàng]？
lines.id: What's the weather like tomorrow?
lines.literal: tomorrow — weather — how.

lines.speaker: 李明:
lines.text: [听说|Tīngshuō][要|yào][下雨|xià yǔ]。[可能|Kěnéng][凉快|liángkuai][一点儿|yìdiǎnr]。
lines.id: I hear it's going to rain. It might be a bit cooler.
lines.literal: hear-say — will — fall — rain. maybe — cool — a-little.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [太好了|Tài hǎo le]！[我|Wǒ][最近|zuìjìn][很|hěn][累|lèi]，[睡|shuì][得|de][不|bù][好|hǎo]。
lines.id: Great! I've been really tired lately — I'm not sleeping well.
lines.literal: too — good — (change). I — lately — (prop) — tired, sleep — (marker) — not — good.

lines.speaker: 李明:
lines.text: [你|Nǐ][是不是|shì bu shì][工作|gōngzuò][太|tài][忙|máng][了|le]？
lines.id: Is work too busy for you?
lines.literal: you — be — not — be — work — too — busy — (change).

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [有|Yǒu][一点儿|yìdiǎnr]。[而且|Érqiě][天气|tiānqì][这么|zhème][热|rè]，[我|wǒ][没有|méiyǒu][胃口|wèikǒu]。
lines.id: A bit. Plus, with the weather this hot, I have no appetite.
lines.literal: have — a-little. moreover — weather — this — hot, I — not-have — stomach-mouth.

lines.speaker: 李明:
lines.text: [多|Duō][喝|hē][水|shuǐ]，[早点儿|zǎo diǎnr][休息|xiūxi]。[身体|Shēntǐ][最|zuì][重要|zhòngyào]。
lines.id: Drink lots of water and get to bed early. Your health comes first.
lines.literal: more — drink — water, early — a-bit — rest. body — most — important.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [谢谢|Xièxie][你|nǐ][的|de][关心|guānxīn]。
lines.id: Thanks for caring.
lines.literal: thank — you — (of) — concern.

notes: **[真|zhēn] + adjective + [啊|a]！** — the most natural exclamation: [真热啊|Zhēn rè a]！ it's so hot! Unlike flat 很, 真 really does add emphasis.
**[这么|zhème] = "this, so".** [这么热|zhème rè] this hot, [这么贵|zhème guì] this expensive. Its partner is [那么|nàme] "that, so".
**[是不是|shì bu shì]…？ = "is it that …?"** A question that guesses at a cause. [你是不是很累|Nǐ shì bu shì hěn lèi]？ Are you tired? It sounds caring, not accusing.
**[而且|érqiě] = plus, moreover.** Adds a second reason. Often paired with [不但|búdàn] "not only".
**[多|duō] / [少|shǎo] + verb = do more / do less.** [多喝水|duō hē shuǐ] drink plenty of water, [少吃辣的|shǎo chī là de] cut down on spicy food. A very typically Chinese way to give advice.
**[早点儿|zǎo diǎnr] = a bit earlier.** Same pattern as [便宜一点儿|piányi yìdiǎnr] from Unit 3: adjective + 一点儿 means "a bit more …".
**[身体最重要|Shēntǐ zuì zhòngyào]** — "your health is what matters most". A closing line of advice you'll hear often from Chinese people — well worth memorizing whole.

grammars.title: Weather and seasons
after: ⚠️ **Rain and snow use the verb [下|xià] "fall"**, not a verb of their own: [下雨|xià yǔ], [下雪|xià xuě]. Wind uses [刮|guā] "blow": [刮风|guā fēng].
[今天天气怎么样|Jīntiān tiānqì zěnmeyàng]？ — safe small talk anywhere.

grammars.title: The adjectives you'll need most
after: ⚠️ **[高|gāo] is for people and buildings; for other things, the opposite isn't 矮 but 短 or 低.** For people: 高 ↔ 矮. For long objects: 长 ↔ 短. For prices and temperatures: 高 ↔ 低.
⚠️ Be careful with [胖|pàng] "fat". In China it's far more neutral than in the West, but it's still best not used with people you've just met.

blocks.text: Describing people takes two things: adjectives, and the tact to know which ones you can say out loud. The table below is filtered for both.

head: Aspect
Example sentence
Meaning
rows: She's not very tall. — gentler than 矮
She's interesting, fun to talk to.
[他看起来很年轻|Tā kànqǐlái hěn niánqīng]。
[他看起来很累|Tā kànqǐlái hěn lèi]。

blocks.title: Giving and taking compliments
items: [你的中文很好|Nǐ de Zhōngwén hěn hǎo]！ — Your Mandarin is great! You'll hear this constantly, even after saying three words.
The right answer: **[哪里哪里|Nǎli nǎli]。** or **[还差得远呢|Hái chà de yuǎn ne]。** "I still have a long way to go."
⚠️ Just saying [谢谢|xièxie] is actually fine and increasingly common among young people, but modesty is still seen as more polite.
[你太客气了|Nǐ tài kèqi le]。 — "You're too kind." Used when someone gives too much praise or too many gifts.
[过奖了|Guòjiǎng le]。 — "You flatter me." A more formal version.

head: Taste
Mandarin
Example sentence
rows: [我不能吃辣的|Wǒ bù néng chī là de]。
[这个菜太油了|Zhège cài tài yóu le]。

blocks.title: Judging food without giving offense
items: [很好吃|Hěn hǎochī]！ — Delicious! A compliment that's always welcome.
[味道很特别|Wèidào hěn tèbié]。 — "It has a unique taste." A lifesaver when you don't like it but don't want to lie.
[我吃不了辣的|Wǒ chī bu liǎo là de]。 — I can't handle spicy food.
[我不吃猪肉|Wǒ bù chī zhūròu]。 — I don't eat pork. A must-memorize sentence for Muslim travelers; no explanation needed, and Chinese people are used to hearing it.
[有清真餐厅吗|Yǒu qīngzhēn cāntīng ma]？ — Is there a halal restaurant? [清真|qīngzhēn] is the official word for halal in China, written on the signs of Muslim restaurants.

exercises.prompt: Correct these sentences, then write the correct form in pīnyīn.
items: [北京是很大|Běijīng shì hěn dà]。
[他不很忙|Tā bù hěn máng]。

answers: 很 — 不 — 太 — 很 — 很
小 — 便宜 — 容易 — 近 — 冷 — 慢
